name: Notification channels and categories
plain: Splits alerts into types the person can silence one by one.
meaning: Gives control over each kind of message (promotions vs receipts). It also stops an app turning off everything: a person can mute marketing and keep security alerts.

android.persistence: Channel stays; importance cannot be raised by the app after the first creation
android.revocation: Settings > Apps > Notifications > channels; deleting a channel keeps user settings
android.note: Android 8 requires a channel for every notification

ios.prompt_ui: Per app settings plus in-app settings link
ios.persistence: Per app; categories only describe actions, not user visible channels
ios.api_surface: iOS has no per-type user controls beyond the app's own settings page and grouping

limits.headline: Can sort its alerts into types you can silence one by one
limits.user_action: You open the app's notification settings and switch a type on or off
can: Split alerts into types, like messages, promotions and reminders
Let you change sound, vibration and importance for each type
Link you from inside the app to its notification settings
cannot: Turn a type back on after you switched it off
Skip channels on Android 8 or later; every alert needs one
Change your per type choices without you opening Settings
limits.differs: Android requires a channel for every alert. iPhone uses per app settings plus an in app link.

story.what_it_is: Settings that split an app's alerts into types so you can mute some and keep others.

marketing.name: Notification channels
marketing.pitch: Android lets people control each type of notification for an app, such as promotions versus receipts.

story.for_you: You open an app's alert settings and see switches like Order updates and Promotions. You can silence the noisy kind and keep the useful kind.
story.for_makers: Makers separate marketing from must have alerts to avoid being muted entirely. A well labeled channel keeps people from turning off everything.

use_cases.example: A chat app has separate channels for messages, calls and group mentions.
A food app splits order updates from deals, so you can mute deals.
A game splits event reminders from friend invites and daily rewards.
A bank keeps fraud alerts on a channel that stays on while promos are off.
A news app lets you choose breaking news but skip opinion pieces.
A shopping app keeps order alerts apart from sales alerts.
A security camera app marks door alarms as high priority and routine clips as low.

risks: Promos hidden in an important channel
story.android_note: Android 8 and up requires a channel for every alert.
story.ios_note: iOS has categories plus a link to the app's own settings.

technical_bounds: Android cannot downgrade user chosen importance upward
iOS lacks a user-visible per-type switch

abuse: Hiding promos in a transactional channel

history.change: Notification channels required for every notification
Notification channel groups can be blocked; blocked channels hide in the shade
